column1: # Hand-labelled ground truth for the CVE matcher.
# Each row is one assertion: given this package at this version, must the
# matcher report this CVE or not?
# The expected answers are derived from the affected-version ranges NVD itself
# publishes (printed straight out of data/cve_index.tsv while this file was
# written), not from memory. The matcher's job is to implement those ranges
# faithfully, and this file is what "faithfully" means -- boundary versions,
# gaps between disjoint ranges, distro packaging suffixes, and library package
# names all included, because those are where a matcher silently goes wrong.
# Boundary rows are deliberately over-represented. A matcher that gets the
# middle of a range right and the endpoint wrong reports a patched host as
# vulnerable, which is the failure that destroys trust in a scanner.
